q: Wave motion is a method of transferring energy by successive _____ through the medium.
e: Wave motion is defined as a method of transferring energy by successive disturbances through the medium.

q: In wave motion, the movement of energy takes place without transferring _____.
e: This movement of energy takes place without transferring matter.

q: All waves are produced by a _____ source.
e: All waves are produced by a vibrating source.

q: Energy and _____ are transferred through the medium from the wave source.
e: Energy and momentum are transferred through the medium from the wave source.

q: Mechanical waves need a material medium to propagate and cannot pass through _____.
e: The mechanical waves need material medium to propagate and cannot pass through vacuum.

q: Sound waves and seismic waves are examples of _____ waves.
e: Sound waves and seismic waves, which are produced by an earthquake, are mechanical waves.

q: Electromagnetic waves can pass through vacuum and they do not need _____ for propagation.
e: Electromagnetic waves can pass through vacuum and they do not need medium for propagation.

q: Light waves and X-rays are examples of _____ waves.
e: Light wave and X-rays are electromagnetic waves.

q: When a stone is dropped onto a quiet surface of a pond, the water in the pond does not move from the centre to the _____.
e: The waves spread out carrying energy, but the water in the pond does not move from the centre to the edges.

q: Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on the _____ of particles in the medium.
e: Waves are classified as transverse and longitudinal waves depending on vibration of particles in the medium through which they propagate.

q: If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a _____ wave.
e: If the displacements of particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of the wave, such a wave is called a transverse wave.

q: Waves in a vibrating string are examples of _____ waves.
e: Waves in a vibrating string are transverse waves.

q: If the displacements of particles of the medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a _____ wave.
e: If the displacements of particles of medium are parallel to the direction of the waves, such a wave is called a longitudinal wave.

q: Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are _____ waves.
e: Compressional waves in a slinky coiled spring and sound waves are longitudinal waves.

q: A longitudinal wave is demonstrated by rapidly pushing forth and pulling back at one end of a _____ coiled spring.
e: A longitudinal wave is demonstrated by rapidly pushing forth and pulling back at one end of a slinky coiled spring while another end is fixed.

q: Water waves are a good example of _____ waves.
e: Some waves in nature exhibit a combination of transverse and longitudinal waves. Water waves are good example of combinational waves.

q: The highest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave _____.
e: The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position are called wave crest and wave trough respectively.

q: The lowest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave _____.
e: The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position are called wave crest and wave trough respectively.

q: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests or two consecutive wave troughs is called _____.
e: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) two consecutive wave troughs is called wavelength.

q: The SI unit of wavelength is the _____.
e: The unit of wavelength in SI unit is metre (m).

q: Generally, the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of the same _____.
e: Generally the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of same phase.

q: The number of complete waves passing a point per second is called the _____ of the wave.
e: The number of complete waves passing a point per second of a vibrating source is also called frequency.

q: The SI unit of frequency is the _____.
e: The SI unit of frequency is hertz (Hz).

q: One hertz is equal to one complete _____ per second.
e: One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second.

q: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests is called the _____ of a wave.
e: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) the time required for one complete vibration is called period of a wave.

q: The unit of period is the _____.
e: The unit of period is the second (s).

q: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the _____.
e: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency.

q: The mathematical relationship between period $T$ and frequency $f$ is _____.
e: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency, thus $T = \frac{1}{f}$.

q: The amplitude of a wave is the _____ value of displacement of a vibrating particle.
e: The amplitude of a wave is the maximum value of displacement of vibrating particle.

q: The velocity of a wave is the _____ with which a wave crest travels.
e: Velocity of wave is the speed with which a wave crest travels.

q: The unit of wave velocity is _____.
e: The unit of wave velocity is metre per second ($\text{m s}^{-1}$).

q: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine or cosine graphs, therefore they can be called _____ waves.
e: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine (or) cosine graphs. Therefore they can be called sine waves.

q: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave is given by the equation _____.
e: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave is $v = f \lambda$.

q: A displacement-distance graph describes the displacement of all particles at a particular instant of _____.
e: A displacement-distance graph describes the displacement of all particles at a particular instant of time.

q: In a displacement-distance graph, the displacement of the particle is plotted on the _____.
e: Note that displacement of particle is plotted on y-axis and distance moved by the wave is on x-axis.

q: A displacement-time graph describes the displacement of a particle of a certain position as a function of _____ taken to travel by a wave.
e: A displacement-time graph describes the displacement of particle of a certain position as a function of time taken to travel by a wave.

q: In a displacement-time graph, the time interval is plotted on the _____.
e: Note that displacement of particle is on Y axis and time interval is on X axis.

q: The ripple tank is a convenient piece of apparatus for demonstrating the properties of _____.
e: The ripple tank is a convenient piece of apparatus for demonstrating the properties of waves.

q: The surface that joins all the points of the same phase is called a _____.
e: The surface that joins all the points of same phase is called wavefront.

q: The turning back of waves when they strike an obstacle is called the _____ of waves.
e: When a series of wave strike an obstacle, they are turned back. This turning back of waves is called reflection of waves.

q: When waves strike a straight barrier, the angle of incidence is _____ to the angle of reflection.
e: When waves strike a straight barrier, the waves are reflected from the barrier. The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.

q: In the reflection of waves, the wavelength and velocity of the wave remain _____.
e: The wavelength and velocity of the wave remain constant in reflection of wave.

q: When plane waves strike a concave barrier, the reflected waves _____.
e: When waves strike a concave barrier, waves converge after striking.

q: When plane waves strike a convex barrier, the reflected waves _____.
e: When waves strike a convex barrier, waves diverge after striking.

q: The speed of water waves depends on the _____ of water.
e: The speed of water waves depends on the depth of water.

q: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water, the velocity of the wave is _____ and the wavelength is shorter.
e: When water waves pass from deep to shallow water the velocity of wave is lesser and the wavelength is shorter.

q: A change in direction of waves when they are incident to the boundary with an angle is called _____.
e: When waves are incident to the boundary with an angle, the direction of the waves changes. Such a change in direction is called refraction.

q: In refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but the _____ remains the same.
e: It can be noticed that in refraction, the wavelength and velocity change but frequency remains the same.

q: Diffraction is the spreading of waves from the straight-on direction through a gap or around an _____.
e: Diffraction is the spreading of waves from the straight-on direction through a gap (or) moves around an obstacle.

q: In the diffraction of water waves, the wider the gap, the _____ the waves spread out.
e: In Figure 7.17 the wider the gap, the less the waves spread out.

q: In the diffraction of water waves, the narrower the gap, the _____ the waves spread out.
e: In Figure 7.18 the narrower the gap, the more the waves spread out.

q: In diffraction, the wavelength of the wave does not _____.
e: Note that the wavelength does not change during diffraction.

q: Sound is a form of _____ that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium.
e: Sound is a form of energy that is transferred from one place to another in a certain medium.

q: Sound wave is produced by a _____ object placed in a medium.
e: Sound wave is produced by a vibrating object placed in a medium.

q: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and _____ like longitudinal waves.
e: Sound wave propagates as a series of compression and rarefaction like longitudinal waves on a vibrating spring.

q: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate and cannot travel through _____.
e: Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound waves need a medium to propagate. Sound wave cannot travel through vacuum.

q: The compression region in a sound wave has _____ pressure.
e: The compression region has higher pressure.

q: When the vibrating object moves back, the molecules are spread out and _____ is created.
e: When the object moves back, the molecules are spread out and rarefaction is created and the pressure of that region is low.

q: Sound energy is transferred through the medium by successive pressure changes without moving the _____ as a whole.
e: Sound energy is transferred through the medium by the successive pressure changes among the adjacent parts without moving the medium as a whole.

q: When sound waves enter the ear, they strike the _____ and make it vibrate.
e: When waves enter the ear, they strike the ear drum and make it vibrate.

q: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than 20 Hz and lower than _____ Hz.
e: The average person can only hear sound that has a frequency higher than 20 Hz and lower than 20 000 Hz.

q: The interval of frequency from 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz is called the _____ range.
e: This interval of frequency is called the audible range (or) hearing range.

q: Sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz are called _____.
e: Sound waves with frequencies greater than 20 000 Hz are called ultrasounds.

q: Sound waves with frequencies under 20 Hz are called _____.
e: Some objects vibrating with frequencies under 20 Hz produces sound which cannot be heard by human. This is called infrasound.

q: Elephants can communicate with _____.
e: On the other hand, elephants can communicate with infrasound.

q: Dogs, bats, and dolphins can hear and communicate with _____.
e: It is found that, by experiments: dog, bat and dolphin can hear the ultrasound and they communicate with it.

q: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the _____ of the medium.
e: Generally, the speed of sound depends on the density of the medium.

q: The denser the medium is, the _____ the speed of sound because the particles are tightly bound together.
e: The denser the medium is, the greater the speed because the particles of the medium are tightly bound together.

q: At 0°C, the speed of sound in air is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: At 0°C the speed of sound in air is 332 $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

q: Whenever the air temperature increases by 1°C, the speed of sound will increase by _____ %.
e: Whenever the air temperature increases by 1°C, speed of sound will increase by 0.2 %.

q: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ with a temperature rise of one degree.
e: In air medium, the speed of sound increases by 0.6 $\text{m s}^{-1}$ with temperature rise by one degree.

q: The speed of sound in air can be expressed by the formula $v = 332 \sqrt{\frac{T}{273}}$, where $T$ is given in _____.
e: Here $T$ is given in K and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

q: The approximate relation for the speed of sound in air with temperature $T$ in Kelvin is $v = $ _____.
e: The above relation can be approximated by $v = 332 + 0.6(T - 273)$.

q: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in pure water at 0°C is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: Table 7.1 lists the speed of sound in pure water at 0°C as 1404 $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

q: According to the textbook, the speed of sound in copper at 20°C is _____ $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
e: Table 7.1 lists the speed of sound in copper at 20°C as 3560 $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
